english: to stare at / look up at
usage: Why do you keep staring at me?
Common slightly annoyed line when someone's gaze lingers
I blankly stared up at the ceiling
쳐다보다 often implies looking up or fixed staring
examples: 모르는 사람이 저를 계속 쳐다봐서 좀 불편했어요
A stranger kept staring at me, so I felt a bit uncomfortable
Everyday situation on the subway or street
다들 휴대폰만 쳐다보고 있어요
Everyone is just staring at their phones
휴대폰만 쳐다보다 = glued to one's phone
고양이가 창밖을 가만히 쳐다보고 있었어요
The cat was quietly staring out the window
가만히 쳐다보다 = stare still/intently
nuance: 쳐다보다 is the everyday word for looking directly or fixedly at something, often upward or with a hint of staring. It can feel neutral ('look at') but in person-to-person contexts it easily carries a slightly negative 'why are you staring' tone, so soften it or use 보다 if you just mean a quick glance.
mistakes: Using 쳐다보다 for casually 'watching' TV or a movie — that is 보다, not 쳐다보다.

usage: 바라보다 = look at something at a distance, calmly
We looked at each other and smiled
examples: 퇴근길에 한강을 바라보면 마음이 편해져요
Gazing at the Han River on the way home from work calms me down
Very natural Seoul daily-life sentence
그냥 멍하니 하늘을 바라보고 있었어요
I was just blankly gazing at the sky
멍하니 바라보다 = stare off vacantly
우리는 같은 곳을 바라보고 있어요
We are looking in the same direction
Often used figuratively about shared goals/values
nuance: 바라보다 is to look at something usually at a distance and with a calm, often emotional or contemplative feeling — gazing at scenery, a person, or the future. Unlike 쳐다보다, it almost never feels aggressive, so it's the safe choice for 'looking fondly at' someone or something.
mistakes: Don't use 바라보다 for reading small text or inspecting something up close — use 보다 or 살펴보다.

usage: I looked over the contract carefully
Look around carefully before you cross
examples: 집을 계약하기 전에 옵션을 꼼꼼히 살펴보세요
Before signing for the place, examine the options carefully
Very useful when renting in Korea
증상을 좀 더 살펴보고 약을 드릴게요
Let me examine your symptoms a bit more and then give you medicine
Doctor/pharmacy context
메뉴를 천천히 살펴보고 주문할게요
I'll look over the menu slowly and then order
Polite thing to say to a server
nuance: 살펴보다 means to look at something attentively to check or understand it — documents, a room, symptoms, your surroundings. It carries a sense of care and thoroughness, so it's the go-to verb whenever you 'review' or 'check over' something rather than just glance.
mistakes: Don't confuse with 둘러보다: 살펴보다 emphasizes careful inspection, while 둘러보다 is more like a casual look-around.

usage: I'll look into it / check on it
Extremely common at work and in service situations
It had been so long that they didn't recognize me
examples: 비자 연장 방법을 좀 알아봐야 해요
I need to look into how to extend my visa
Practical life-admin sentence
가격을 여기저기 알아보고 제일 싼 데서 샀어요
I checked prices here and there and bought from the cheapest place
알아보다 = shop around / research
머리를 자르니까 친구가 저를 못 알아봤어요
After I got a haircut my friend didn't recognize me
Recognition meaning
nuance: 알아보다 has two everyday meanings: to investigate or look into something (information, prices, options) and to recognize someone or something. The 'look into' sense is one of the most useful verbs in Korea — '제가 알아볼게요' is how you say you'll check on a matter.
mistakes: For 'recognize', use 알아보다, not 알다 — 알다 is just 'to know'.

english: to watch over / keep an eye on
usage: Let's keep an eye on it a bit longer for now
I quietly watched over them from a distance
examples: 상태가 어떤지 며칠 더 지켜봅시다
Let's watch the condition for a few more days
Doctor or vet saying 'let's monitor it'
부모님이 항상 저를 지켜봐 주셔서 든든해요
It's reassuring that my parents always watch over me
Warm, protective sense
환율을 며칠 지켜보다가 환전할 거예요
I'll watch the exchange rate for a few days and then exchange money
Practical for residents managing money
nuance: 지켜보다 means to watch something continuously over time — to monitor, keep an eye on, or 'wait and see.' It often implies care or caution, so it shows up constantly in medical advice ('let's monitor it'), parenting, and decisions you want to postpone until the situation develops.
mistakes: Don't use 지켜보다 for watching a single show or event for entertainment — that's 보다.

usage: The exact phrase to tell a shop clerk you're just browsing
examples: 사기 전에 매장을 한 바퀴 둘러봤어요
I looked around the store once before buying
한 바퀴 둘러보다 = take a look around
새 동네로 이사 와서 주변을 둘러보고 있어요
I moved to a new neighborhood, so I'm looking around the area
Useful for newcomers exploring their area
전시회를 둘러보는 데 한 시간쯤 걸렸어요
It took about an hour to look around the exhibition
둘러보는 데 ~ 걸리다 = takes ~ to look around
nuance: 둘러보다 is to glance around a place broadly — a store, a neighborhood, an exhibition. When a clerk asks if you need help, '그냥 둘러볼게요' or '둘러보는 거예요' is the natural way to say 'I'm just browsing.' It's casual and carries no sense of close inspection.
mistakes: 둘러보다 is for surveying a whole space, not for inspecting one item closely — use 살펴보다 for that.

english: to peer into / look closely at
usage: I've been staring down at my phone all day
휴대폰을 들여다보다 = peer down at one's phone
examples: 문제가 뭔지 제가 한번 들여다볼게요
Let me take a close look at what the problem is
Figurative: examine an issue in detail
아이가 어항을 신기하게 들여다보고 있었어요
The child was peering curiously into the fish tank
Looking into something with interest
서류를 한참 들여다봤는데도 이해가 안 됐어요
Even after poring over the document for a while, I didn't understand
한참 들여다보다 = study/pore over
nuance: 들여다보다 is to look closely into something — a container, a screen, or a problem — usually bending or leaning in. It suggests focused, up-close attention, so it works both literally (peering into a bag) and figuratively (examining an issue in depth).
mistakes: Don't swap with 둘러보다: 들여다보다 is a close look into one thing, 둘러보다 is a broad look around a space.

usage: You shouldn't peek at someone else's phone
엿보다 carries a sneaky, secret nuance
I peeked through the crack in the door
문틈으로 엿보다 = peek through a gap
examples: 옆 사람 답안지를 엿보면 부정행위예요
Peeking at the next person's answer sheet is cheating
Exam context, clearly negative
커튼 사이로 밖을 엿봤어요
I peeked outside through the gap in the curtains
Secretly looking out
이 책에서는 조선시대 생활을 엿볼 수 있어요
This book lets you get a glimpse of life in the Joseon era
Figurative: get a glimpse into
nuance: 엿보다 means to look at something secretly or furtively — peeking through a gap, spying, or sneaking a look at someone's private things. It almost always sounds sneaky or improper, though figuratively '~을 엿볼 수 있다' is a neutral way to say something 'offers a glimpse into' a world or era.
mistakes: Don't use 엿보다 for openly looking at something — it specifically implies secrecy.

usage: Why are you glaring at me like that?
He glared with his eyes wide open
examples: 새치기한 사람을 다들 노려봤어요
Everyone glared at the person who cut in line
Common social-irritation scene
강아지가 낯선 사람을 가만히 노려보고 있었어요
The dog was quietly glaring at the stranger
Animals/people sensing a threat
화가 났는지 저를 한참 노려봤어요
Maybe they were angry — they glared at me for a while
Expresses hostility/anger
nuance: 노려보다 is to stare at someone with anger or hostility — to glare. It's strong and clearly negative, signaling irritation, threat, or a challenge. Use it only when you really mean an angry stare; for a plain look use 보다, and for an uncomfortable lingering look use 쳐다보다.
mistakes: 노려보다 is never neutral — don't use it where English 'look at' would do.

usage: 쓱 훑어보다 = give a quick once-over
I skimmed through the article quickly
examples: 출근하면서 뉴스를 훑어봐요
I skim the news on my way to work
Daily commuter habit
계약서를 훑어보지만 말고 꼼꼼히 읽으세요
Don't just skim the contract — read it carefully
Contrasts skimming vs careful reading
면접관이 제 이력서를 쭉 훑어봤어요
The interviewer skimmed down my resume
쭉 훑어보다 = run one's eyes over
nuance: 훑어보다 means to run your eyes over something quickly to get the gist — skimming a menu, an article, or a document. It implies speed and a lack of deep attention, so it pairs naturally with 쓱 or 쭉, and contrasts with 살펴보다 (careful inspection).
mistakes: Don't use 훑어보다 when you mean to read or check something thoroughly — use 살펴보다 or 읽다.

usage: Don't eavesdrop on other people's conversations
엿듣다 = listen in secretly (ㄷ irregular: 듣다→들어요)
Often softened with 우연히 = by chance
examples: 카페에서 옆자리 얘기를 본의 아니게 엿들었어요
At the cafe I unintentionally overheard the next table's talk
본의 아니게 = not on purpose
문 앞에서 엿듣다가 들켰어요
I got caught eavesdropping at the door
엿듣다가 들키다 = get caught eavesdropping
남의 통화를 엿듣는 건 예의가 아니에요
Listening in on someone's call isn't polite
Note ㄷ→ㄹ shift: 엿듣는
nuance: 엿듣다 is the listening counterpart of 엿보다 — to overhear or eavesdrop, usually secretly. Like its English equivalent it sounds improper, so people often soften it with 우연히 ('by chance') or 본의 아니게 ('unintentionally') to make clear it wasn't deliberate. It follows the ㄷ-irregular: 듣다 → 들어요.
mistakes: Remember the ㄷ irregular: it's 엿들어요 / 엿들었어요, never 엿듣어요.

english: to understand (by hearing) / catch what is said
usage: I couldn't catch what you were saying
The single most useful phrase for learners (ㄷ irregular)
If you speak slowly I can understand
examples: 한국어를 다 알아듣지는 못하지만 조금은 알아들어요
I can't catch all the Korean, but I understand a little
Honest learner self-description
발음이 빨라서 하나도 못 알아들었어요
The pronunciation was so fast I couldn't catch a thing
하나도 못 알아듣다 = not catch a single word
강아지도 자기 이름은 알아들어요
Even the dog understands its own name
Light everyday usage
nuance: 알아듣다 is to understand something you hear — to catch or make out spoken words. It's distinct from 이해하다 (to comprehend a concept): 알아듣다 is specifically about successfully receiving speech. For anyone living in Korea, '못 알아들었어요' and '천천히 말해 주세요' are everyday survival lines. It follows the ㄷ-irregular: 듣다 → 들어요.
mistakes: ㄷ irregular: say 알아들어요 / 알아들었어요, not 알아듣어요. Also don't replace it with 이해하다 when you mean catching spoken words.
